newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end lower for sixth straight day.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end lower for sixth straight day.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed lower for the sixth straight session as foreign investors continued to stay away, waiting for labor strife to end, traders said.
The market's leading 19-share index slipped 0.78 percent to end at 6,200.85 as 35 million shares traded worth 2.6 billion bolivars ($5.5 million).
"Local players, who don't really move the market anyway, are indifferent, while foreign investors, who do move the market, are looking elsewhere," said one trader.
Analysts fear growing public sector wage claims may bust Venezuela's fragile fiscal balance and send inflation soaring beyond the government's projected 25 percent for 1997.
Until the outlook becomes clearer, foreign investors will continue to stay away from Venezuelan equities, analysts said.
Among traded issues, 22 fell, 11 rose and nine closed unchanged. Trading volume swelled as 22 million Corimon B shares changed hands. The stock closed flat at 9.00 bolivars.
